input.title: Reinvestment: R&D and capex, latest year

items: NVDA's revenue rose from $26.9B in FY2022 to $215.9B in FY2026, while AMD's rose from $16.4B in FY2021 to $34.6B in FY2025.
NVDA's YoY growth peaked at 125.9% in FY2024 and was 65.5% in FY2026; AMD's was −3.9% in FY2023 and 34.3% in FY2025.
NVDA's R&D was $18.5B (8.6% of revenue) in FY2026, down from 27.2% in FY2023; AMD's was $8.1B (23.4% of revenue) in FY2025.
Free cash flow was $96.7B for NVDA in FY2026 and $6.7B for AMD in FY2025, with capex of $6.0B and $974M respectively.
NVDA's buybacks were $40.1B in FY2026 and AMD's were $1.3B in FY2025. NVDA paid $974M in dividends, while AMD's dividends are not reported.

AMD vs NVIDIA: how fast they grow, and what pays for it

Five fiscal years of revenue, growth, reinvestment and free cash flow; the two companies' years are lined up by position, not by calendar.

Takeaways

  • NVIDIA's revenue went from $26.9B (FY2022) to $215.9B (FY2026), while AMD's went from $16.4B (FY2021) to $34.6B (FY2025).
  • AMD's revenue growth was −3.9% in FY2023; NVIDIA's was 0.2% in FY2023, and NVIDIA's peak was 125.9% in FY2024.
  • R&D was 23.4% of revenue at AMD (FY2025) and 8.6% at NVIDIA (FY2026), even though NVIDIA's R&D was $18.5B against AMD's $8.1B.
  • Free cash flow reached $6.7B at AMD (FY2025) and $96.7B at NVIDIA (FY2026), against capex of $974M and $6.0B.
  • NVIDIA's long-term debt to equity moved from 0.41× to 0.05× over its range; AMD's was 0.04× in FY2025.

Not financial advice.

Source: each company's 10-K filings, AMD FY2021 to FY2025 and NVIDIA FY2022 to FY2026. Dividends paid are n/r for AMD; cash runway is n/m for both.
